From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cascading VLAN cutover & orchestration plan for Private deployments

Team / Acme ops,

Attaching an initial orchestration proposal for the staged VLAN cutover we discussed for the Private deployment clusters in us-west-2. Goal is a low-risk, observable sequence that allows us to:
- Move subnet mappings for service groups without a full restart of inference processes
- Preserve KV cache affinity where possible and avoid unnecessary cache invalidations
- Enforce version pinning at the edge so model-serving binaries remain pinned during the window

Key asks up front:
1) Confirm a 4-hour maintenance window where Acme can accept brief TCP connection drains and BGP flaps (proposed: 2026-06-25 02:00-06:00 UTC).
2) Network team to pre-stage VLANs and route maps in 'staged' mode; we will toggle them on in sequence.
3) Dev/Infra: prepare canary node group (10% traffic) and a rollback ladder (canary -> regional -> global).
4) SRE: define exact rollback criteria (error-rate thresholds, p95 latency delta, request-drop rates).

I've included: vlan-rollout-matrix.xlsx (step-by-step cutover table), seq-diagram.pdf (visual sequence), runbook-v1.md (draft runbook).

Primary risks called out in the workbook: DB control-plane migration ordering, firewall rule priorities causing transient 503s, and accidental KV cache eviction on model upgrade. The draft runbook includes a pre-check checklist and explicit post-cutover verification (token-level traces and model-serving latency histogram).

Please reply with two things: a) which blackout window you can accept, and b) any missing preflight checks we should add before starting the canary.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Jonas — good outline, added inline notes below.

On Mon, Jun 15, 2026 at 09:12 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team / Acme ops,
> 
> Attaching an initial orchestration proposal for the staged VLAN cutover we discussed for the Private deployment clusters in us-west-2.

Inline notes (high level):
- Canary sizing: instead of 10% I recommend 3 staged canaries: 1% (smoke), 10% (warm), 30% (full region). We need to validate cache-warm hit rate after each stage.
- Rollback criteria: add a hard stop if p95 latency increases by >40% or error-rate increases by >2x sustained for 5 minutes. Also require a KV-cache-hit threshold — if hit-rate drops >15% post-cut, abort and resume previous routing.
- Model pinning: ensure the runtime reads a pin file (pinned_model.txt) at startup and we do not overwrite it during the VLAN toggle. Add a post-cut job that verifies model hashes match the pinned release.
- DB control-plane: add explicit ordering: control-plane write followers -> control-plane leaders -> read-only replicas. Any control-plane migration must be done in a separate, pre-approved step (not during VLAN toggle).

I'll add these to runbook-v1.md and push a delta. Also proposing we run a rehearsed dry-run inside the staging VPC this week.

Mina
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Cascading VLAN cutover & orchestration plan for Private deployments

Adding network specifics and a couple of gating items from infra: 

1) IP / subnet mapping: we will map the new service VLANs to the same L3 prefixes where possible to avoid ARP churn. For the clusters in question the target prefixes are 10.42.0.0/16 (edge), 10.43.0.0/16 (core).
2) BGP adjacency: Acme needs to be ready to accept short-lived route withdraws. We'll sequence route advertisements: advertise new routes -> withdraw old -> confirm telemetry -> deprecate. Plan a 45s grace for route convergence at each stage.
3) Firewall rule ordering: critical. If we push rule sets in the wrong order we will see transient 502s as connection tracking mismatches. We should push rules in a two-phase commit pattern (stage then activate) and verify with a traffic-sim.
4) MTU considerations: we have jumbo frames enabled on core; ensure that path MTU is verified after VLAN toggle. Packet fragmentation can surface as odd application-level errors.

Gating items for Acme: whitelist our staging IPs (10.100.0.0/24) for the rehearsal and confirm there are no rate-limiting middleboxes that will kill the canary.

Hiro
Network Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick confirmations and the window, Clare. Final alignment below: 

Decisions confirmed:
- Maintenance window: 2026-06-25 02:00-06:00 UTC (Acme confirmed).
- Canary cadence: 1% smoke -> 10% warm -> 30% regional -> full region. We'll hold 15 minutes between each stage for metrics observation.
- Rollback criteria: abort on p95+latency +40% sustained for 5 minutes OR error-rate >2x sustained for 5 minutes OR KV-cache-hit drop >15%.
- Network sequencing: Hiro will perform route advertise/withdraw with 45s convergence parity; Acme will accept brief BGP withdraws.
- Preflight checks: staging IP whitelist (10.100.0.0/24) granted for rehearsal; Dev to run traffic-sim and firewall-stage verification.
- Post-cut verification: security/NAC check by Acme; we will deliver the 15-minute token-level trace and a short telemetry digest.

Action items and owners:
- Hiro: finalize the route playbook and firewall two-phase commit steps (due: 2026-06-22).
- Mina: push runbook-v1.md updates (canary sizing + rollback criteria) and create a delta PR (due: 2026-06-21).
- Dev: schedule rehearsal in staging, run traffic-sim and report results to the thread (due: 2026-06-23).
- Jonas: prepare final runbook link + DocuSign envelope and circulate to Acme (done by 2026-06-21 morning).

Attachments referenced: vlan-rollout-matrix.xlsx, seq-diagram.pdf, runbook-v1.md (latest will be in the Drive link). DocuSign link will contain Acme's maintenance consent.

If there are no objections I will send the DocuSign and mark the rehearsal slot in calendar tomorrow.
